issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as both messageOnFeed() (declared in the UML and earlier text) and getFeedingSound() (used in the task descriptions, feedAllAnimals description, and the song template). The provided solution implements messageOnFeed(), while parts of the problem text (and the song template) instruct students to call getFeedingSound(). This naming mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and call and may cause implementations or tests to fail if students follow the wrong name.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Either: (A) change all references in the problem statement and templates from getFeedingSound() to messageOnFeed(), matching the UML and solution; or (B) rename the abstract method in Animal and all implementations to getFeedingSound(), and update the solution and templates accordingly. Ensure the song template and feedAllAnimals description reference the same method name students must implement.

issues.description: The problem statement refers to the same animal feeding method using two different identifiers: 'messageOnFeed()' (used in the UML and in the Animal description) and 'getFeedingSound()' (used in the per-animal task descriptions for expected return values). The solution and intended API implement 'messageOnFeed()'. This inconsistency in the problem text can confuse students about which method they must implement and which name tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across all artifacts. Replace all occurrences of 'getFeedingSound()' in the problem statement with 'messageOnFeed()', or alternatively rename the abstract method in the solution/template to 'getFeedingSound()'. Ensure the UML, tests, template, and example usages all use the same identifier (recommended: 'messageOnFeed()' to match the UML and solution).
